headline: Amazon Web Services chief Matt Garman says AI bubble fears do not worry him because most demand comes from workloads that will not go away.
score_reason: Keeps the pool score: a revealing view from the largest cloud provider, but it is one executive's opinion.
importance_line: What changed is that a leading cloud executive publicly rejected the bubble worry just as others warned of a peak, which matters first to savers whose funds hold AI shares, then to investors judging AI spending, and the doubt is that this is the view of an executive whose unit earns money from AI demand.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports that Matt Garman, chief executive of Amazon's cloud unit Amazon Web Services (AWS), said on an Andreessen Horowitz podcast that "we feel really good about the spend we're making now", arguing that AWS spreads its capacity across many customers and that most of its usage is core computing, storage and AI inference (running trained models). The article adds that bubble talk has returned as Nvidia, AMD, Marvell and Micron shares hit records, and that investor Ray Dalio said this week that AI speculation may be nearing its peak.
notes: Read the original page in full. The Dalio comment is relayed by Yahoo Finance.
